title: A temperature with getters
description:
Write an object whose properties convert themselves.

```
const t = new Temperature(100);
t.fahrenheit        // 212
t.fahrenheit = 32;
t.celsius           // 0
t.kelvin = -5       // throws RangeError: below absolute zero
`${t}`              // "0.0 °C"
```
hints: `get fahrenheit() { return this.#celsius * 9 / 5 + 32; }` and `set fahrenheit(f) { this.celsius = (f - 32) * 5 / 9; }`: going through the `celsius` setter keeps the check in one place (lesson 7.02).
With `toPrimitive`, `t + 0` and `t > 50` use the number, and template strings use the text.
requirements: Store only Celsius, in a private field. `celsius`, `fahrenheit` and `kelvin` are get/set pairs.
Setting a value below absolute zero throws a `RangeError`.
`[Symbol.toPrimitive](hint)` gives the number of degrees Celsius for `"number"` and the text above otherwise.
stretch: Add `static fromFahrenheit(f)` and make `Temperature` instances sortable with `.sort((a, b) => a - b)`.
